Proceed autonomously following docs/reusable/engineering-manager.md: your own worktree, a plan doc first, GPT Sol on the plan and at the end of every stage, land on dev. Do not deploy.  CONTEXT. An audit of all 89 docs/postmortems/ on 2026-09-06 found roughly **ninety** prevention recommendations still unbuilt out of about 230 extracted. Most are habits or are too big for one sitting. These are the ones that are small, mechanical, and turn a habit into a check — which is the argument of docs/plans/260905b-improve-the-codebase-third-sweep.md § T2.1, and the reason that plan gives for preferring a check to a sentence every time.  Each item below is **its own stage**: a red test, then the fix, then a review. They touch disjoint files. **Verify each one is still unbuilt before you build it** — a deferral is a claim and it decays, and on 2026-09-06 six of about forty such claims turned out to be already done, already deliberate, or aimed at code that had been deleted. Two of the items below have already been checked for you; the rest have not. If an item turns out to be built, say so in the plan doc, do not build a second copy, and move to the next.  --- STAGE 1 — `componentDidCatch(error: unknown)` (from 260906c-safe-helper-private) --- Verified 2026-09-06: three boundaries still declare `error: Error` — src/web/AppBoundary.tsx:52, src/web/LazyPage.tsx:107, and src/web/FeatureBoundary.tsx. React can hand those anything that was thrown, so `error.name` compiles and can blow up at runtime. **Also verified: the main class fix already landed** — `nameOfThrown` is exported at src/web/log-buffer.ts:407 and LazyPage.tsx already uses it. So this is belt-and-braces, and the value is that `strict` refuses the unsafe read rather than a sweep test noticing it later. Retype to `unknown`, fix what the compiler then objects to using the existing helper, and cover a genuinely non-Error throw with a test that goes red first. Small: do not refactor error handling generally.  --- STAGE 2 — the `mayPassThrough` cross-check (from 260901d-409-404-as-500) --- That postmortem's own words: "Not built." An allowlist is blind to routes, so a 409 or 404 can surface as a 500. It asks for a static check that the `mayPassThrough` allowlist and the route classes actually agree. Find both lists, work out how they can disagree, and write the check that fails when they do — then prove it by making them disagree.  --- STAGE 3 — count and log when the JSON repair fires (from 260906b-model-emits-comma-anyway) --- `dropTrailingCommas` silently repairs malformed model JSON, so "the model got the format wrong" is an invisible tax rather than a rate anybody can watch. Log or count when it fires. Read docs/project/logging.md first — anything in a request path goes through src/log.ts, a `console.log` there is a bug, and **never log article prose or model output**. Count and classify; do not log the payload. That postmortem lists two other items (quarantine the raw answer on parse failure, a comma warning in every prompt's schema section) — the second is prompt-wide and is not yours tonight; judge the first on cost and say why in the plan doc if you skip it.  --- STAGE 4 — pick one more, and say why --- Read the "Recorded, not built" / "still open" sections across docs/postmortems/ and choose **one** further item that is (a) genuinely still unbuilt, verified in the tree, (b) achievable in one stage, and (c) not in a file another session is likely to be in tonight. Justify the choice in the plan doc against the ones you rejected. Candidates the audit flagged, none verified: a conflict-marker / `db:chain` guard (**already being done tonight by another session — do not take it**), fixtures captured from the Stripe vendor rather than cast with `as unknown as`, and a deploy-time probe that makes one real embedding call. **Do not take anything that touches a defence** (docs/project/security-map.md § Where the defences physically live) — an unattended run does not edit one; write it up instead.  --- ACROSS ALL STAGES --- **Mutate the finished code at the end of each stage and check the suite notices.** Red-first only tests the diff. That is the whole point of this batch.  Merge origin/dev before you start and again before you push. If the suite is red, re-run the failing files one at a time — this box goes red from contention. doc-links is currently red on dev from another agent's in-flight plan doc and is not yours.  Several sessions are live tonight in src/jobs.ts, src/routes.ts, src/web/styles.css, src/web/App.tsx and the extraction path. Keep edits targeted, re-read immediately before editing, and never rewrite a shared file.  WRITE IT UP. At the end, add a short section to your plan doc listing which items you verified as already built or stale, because that list is worth as much as the ones you built — it is the input to the next docs/reusable/improve-the-codebase.md sweep, and docs/plans/260906i-sweep-for-missed-work-across-feedback-reports-worktrees-and-sessions.md records why.
